title: Displayed Material (Print Only)

illustrates.quote: Displayed material refers to text set off by blank lines and/or a different margin.

blocks.features: Boxed print-only mock-up: a plain paragraph, then one sentence ('The fields are awash in a sea of blue.') set off on its own indented line with blank space above and below and shaded in the source image, then the paragraph resumes -- illustrating 'displayed' material (BANA 1.4.5). No braille is given for this example.

print.notes: Explicitly captioned '(Print Only)' in the source; confirmed against the PDF page image (p.21): a boxed print excerpt only, no accompanying braille box.

resolution: Both runs agree: print-only, no braille. Modeled as a single 'other' block (no real transcribable content) since this sample exists to show a PRINT layout convention (displayed vs. embedded material), not a print-to-braille correspondence; Emboss has no concept of 'displayed material' as a print-side visual cue distinct from ordinary body text (there is nothing in the braille to build toward). status: no-braille (braille.width is null).
